answer: A reputation ledger that only counts work backed by a bonded stake makes fake identities expensive: each new agent must lock a deposit that is slashed if peers catch it lying, so spawning a thousand onyx-dark sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. A violet badge of verified history then accumulates only from completed jobs, and a nebula of small independent attestations, not one central gatekeeper, confirms each claim. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking a whole economy of trusted histories costs more than the fraud returns.
